hist-20c-01-c3.text: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum. Documenting Numbers of Victims of the Holocaust and Nazi Persecution. Holocaust Encyclopedia, United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.
hist-20c-01-c3.quote: The Nazis and their allies and collaborators killed six million Jewish people.
hist-20c-01-c3.claim: The Holocaust was the systematic murder of 6 million Jews

hist-20c-02-c2.text: history.state.gov. Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian. history.state.gov.
hist-20c-02-c2.quote: The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 was a direct and dangerous confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War and was the moment when the two superpowers came closest to nuclear conflict.
hist-20c-02-c2.claim: The Cuban Missile Crisis (October 1962), when Soviet nuclear missiles were discovered in Cuba, brought the world the closest it has ever come to nuclear war.

hist-20c-02-c2.text: history.state.gov. Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian. history.state.gov.
hist-20c-02-c2.quote: On October 4, 1957, the Soviet Union launched the earth’s first artificial satellite, Sputnik-1.
hist-20c-02-c2.claim: The Space Race was Cold War competition by other means: USSR launched Sputnik (1957), the first satellite;

hist-20c-04-c1.text: Energy.gov (2011). Trinity Site - World's First Nuclear Explosion. Energy.gov.
hist-20c-04-c1.quote: The world's first nuclear explosion occurred on July 16, 1945, when a plutonium implosion device was tested at a site located 210 miles south of Los Alamos, New Mexico
hist-20c-04-c1.claim: The first nuclear test (Trinity) occurred on July 16, 1945, in New Mexico.

hist-20c-09-c2.text: history.state.gov. Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian. history.state.gov.
hist-20c-09-c2.quote: The Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962 was a direct and dangerous confrontation between the United States and the Soviet Union during the Cold War and was the moment when the two superpowers came closest to nuclear conflict.
hist-20c-09-c2.claim: In October 1962 the world came closer to nuclear war than at any other moment.

hist-20c-09-c2.text: history.state.gov. Milestones in the History of U.S. Foreign Relations - Office of the Historian. history.state.gov.
hist-20c-09-c2.quote: On October 22, he ordered a naval “quarantine” of Cuba.
hist-20c-09-c2.claim: Kennedy announced a naval 'quarantine' of Cuba on 22 October.

hist-20c-01-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2024). Adolf Hitler. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-20c-01-c2.quote: After the Wall Street Crash of 1929 and the consequent Great Depression, millions of Germans found themselves out of work or on reduced salaries
hist-20c-01-c2.claim: The Wall Street Crash (October 1929) triggered the Great Depression, with global unemployment, bank failures, and social despair.

hist-20c-03-c1.text: Mahatma Gandhi, the missing laureate. NobelPrize.org.
hist-20c-03-c1.quote: Gandhi was nominated in 1937, 1938, 1939, 1947 and, finally, a few days before he was murdered in January 1948.
hist-20c-03-c1.claim: Gandhi was assassinated by a Hindu nationalist on January 30, 1948.

hist-20c-03-c3.quote: He joined the African National Congress in 1944 and was engaged in resistance against the ruling National Party’s apartheid policies after 1948.
hist-20c-03-c3.claim: Apartheid, Afrikaans for 'apartness', was South Africa's system of institutionalized racial segregation, legislated from 1948 by the National Party.

hist-20c-03-c3.quote: Nelson Mandela was released on February 11, 1990.
hist-20c-03-c3.claim: Mandela was released in February 1990, negotiated a peaceful transition to majority rule, and became South Africa's first democratically elected President in 1994.

hist-20c-05-c1.text: Vietnam War U.S. Military Fatal Casualty Statistics. National Archives.
hist-20c-05-c1.quote: The Vietnam Conflict Extract Data File of the Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) Extract Files contains records of 58,220 U.S. military fatal casualties of the Vietnam War.
hist-20c-05-c1.claim: The Vietnam War killed 58,000 Americans and an estimated 3 million Vietnamese (North and South combined).

hist-20c-05-c2.text: Soviet Invasion of Czechoslovakia, 1968. Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State.
hist-20c-05-c2.quote: On August 20, 1968, the Soviet Union led Warsaw Pact troops in an invasion of Czechoslovakia to crack down on reformist trends in Prague.
hist-20c-05-c2.claim: In Czechoslovakia, the Prague Spring, Alexander Dubček's attempt to build 'socialism with a human face', was crushed by Soviet tanks in August.

hist-20c-06-c1.quote: This act, signed into law by President Lyndon Johnson on July 2, 1964, prohibited discrimination in public places, provided for the integration of schools and other public facilities, and made employment discrimination illegal.
hist-20c-06-c1.claim: Key legislation: Civil Rights Act (1964), Voting Rights Act (1965), Fair Housing Act (1968).

hist-20c-06-c3.text: Jack Drescher (2015). Out of DSM: Depathologizing Homosexuality. Behavioral Sciences.
hist-20c-06-c3.quote: In 1973, the American Psychiatric Association (APA) removed the diagnosis of “homosexuality” from the second edition of its Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (DSM).
hist-20c-06-c3.claim: The American Psychiatric Association removed homosexuality from its list of mental illnesses in 1973.

hist-20c-07-c1.quote: He sought to reform communism, and introduced the concepts “glasnost” (openness) and “perestroika” (change).
hist-20c-07-c1.claim: Mikhail Gorbachev (1985-91) launched glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring).

hist-20c-07-c2.text: The Collapse of Communism in Eastern Europe, 1989. Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State.
hist-20c-07-c2.quote: On June 4, as Chinese tanks crushed student-led protests in Beijing, Solidarity delivered a crushing electoral victory.
hist-20c-07-c2.claim: 1989: Solidarity won partially free elections in Poland (June).

hist-20c-08-c3.quote: That started to change in August 1981 with the introduction of the IBM 5150 Personal Computer.
hist-20c-08-c3.claim: Mid-20th century: mainframe computers, then minicomputers, then personal computers (Apple II 1977, IBM PC 1981).

hist-20c-08-c3.text: Barry M. Leiner, Vinton G. Cerf, David D. Clark, Robert E. Kahn, Leonard Kleinrock, Daniel C. Lynch, Jon Postel, Larry G. Roberts, Stephen Wolff (1997). A Brief History of the Internet. Internet Society.
hist-20c-08-c3.quote: One of the more interesting challenges was the transition of the ARPANET host protocol from NCP to TCP/IP as of January 1, 1983.
hist-20c-08-c3.claim: Internet's TCP/IP standardized in 1983; World Wide Web invented 1989; commercialized in 1990s.
